utterances.text: Obviously we don't understand one another. For the SDA to form a government, it would need to have 51 per cent of the votes.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: How do I know how many votes it got? I know who held the various positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who was the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who was the president of the local government?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: The president of the municipality was a Muslim; the chief of police was a Muslim; and the post office and the electricity supply system was held by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you a very clear and precise question. Who was the president of the municipal government?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a businessman at the time. It didn't interest me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, you're talking about facts here. You just said that things were a fact. I'm asking you who was the president of the municipal government.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: He was a teacher, professor, Muhamed -- I can't remember the surname just now. Muhamed. I know that he was a teacher at the high school in Prijedor. I will recall his name a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let me simplify things. So in your view, the president of the municipal government was a member of the Muslim ethnic group. Now let's go back to the tensions that you spoke to. How were they manifesting themselves, when in April you removed your family before the takeover?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely because the tensions had heightened to such a degree that I saw that something would happen. I don't know what. Whether the people would move out or there would be a war, whether there would be a front line or not, one couldn't tell yet at the time. But with the return of the Serb fighters from the Croatian front, they behaved so arrogantly and aggressively that it was dangerous for me, not to mention my wife and child. It was not possible to do business any more normally, and that is why I took that decision. Originally we had planned it for a month. Go on a holiday. Why wait for the summer? Go for a holiday in April, go and visit the family, until we see what happens, I won't leave. And that was the reason. There was shooting in Prijedor as if there was a war on already.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the possibility of war. Who would be waging the war in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: These Serb fighters, these veterans who come from Croatia, whose friend or brother gets killed and then they come to Prijedor to take it out on us. But that is not a war, it's worse than war. He has a gun, a machine-gun; he has all kinds of artillery pieces. And what do I have? And all the other Muslims, what did we have? Did we have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that there was more or less a free market of weapons.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Not more or less. There really was a market.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could anyone buy a weapon?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Anyone who had the money to do so?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Money did not care about ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us go back now for a moment to the Patriotic League. You agree that when a public rally is organised, permission is required. Who granted permission?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: The SUP in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who headed the SUP?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Hasan Talundzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who and why would -- who would withhold permission for holding this peace initiative?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: As of the 30th of April it was not possible because the checkpoints cropped up the very next day. Until April it was possible; that's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in March, was it prohibited?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: We stopped working in March already because there was this forcible takeover of Prijedor. That was on the 15th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: The first attempt or --

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 15th of March, a couple hundred of us rallied in front of the municipality, and then for some reason they changed their minds and they postponed this until they did so by force of arms. So that in March we stopped our concerts and rallies. Kuruzovic would not let us enter the municipality. He organised the TO. Kuruzovic knows what he did around Prijedor. He threatened that he would take me to Croatian Gradiska to see what they had done to Gradiska because of the Ustashas and people like me. And what I had been doing until then? I was engaged in catering and the florist business.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, you mentioned the 15th of March as an attempt to take over power.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How did that manifest itself?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they simply came, the Serbs. They were so powerful. They positioned snipers on the mine administration building behind the municipality. They went into the municipality to come to some sort of an agreement that power should be handed over to them, and they entered. The negotiations started. Who with, I don't know. I wasn't inside; I was in front of the building. And then they saw that people were gathering, and probably the time was still not right for camps, so they postponed the whole thing for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was exactly on the 15th of March, but sometime in March. There was an attempt to take over power in Prijedor in March, I can guarantee that, the first attempt.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: How was it prevented?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Probably thanks to the congregation of this large group of people in front of the municipality. It wasn't prevented, it was postponed.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, you gave a statement in 1994 which you signed, it is 22 pages long, and you spoke in great detail then about many things. Did you ever have a weapon in your life?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What kind?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Hunting weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What kind?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a carbine with a sniper, and a shotgun, a weapon that my father owned for more than 30 years. He was the best-known hunter in Prijedor. And these are weapons that I inherited, because my father died in 1982 and my family made a gift of them to me. But I was never able to get a license from the Serb authorities, from the communist police, who were over my head all my life, ever since I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Beganovic, will you please answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: But this is linked to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that later.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Since you have opened this question, when did your father die?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In 1982? Was there a legal proceeding to establish the succession? Were the weapons lawfully registered as part of his property? I'm asking you, did he have a permit?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a hunter of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When the court ruling came, do you know the procedure for legalising weapons?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you submit a request for the weapons in accordance with the court ruling on succession to be legalised?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I carried the request to SUP. I got a certificate from the hunting society that I'm capable of hunting, that I'm a hunter, and they gave the certificate to SUP but they would never give me one. But they did give me a weapon when I was called up as a reservist to go to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We'll come back to that later. What is the basis for your acquisition of weapons? I'm talking about the legality of holding weapons, of possessing weapons? Did you receive a document granting you approval, in accordance with the law, to hold in your possession any weapons?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I received the court ruling whereby those weapons were passed on to me as part of my inheritance. Everyone knew this, that I inherited those weapons from my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When did you get a request that was rejected?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I received the rejection papers. Even my wife, who was a graduate forestry engineer, and she wanted to gain permission and she was refused too. Rajko Zigic and company would not let her have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that without the permission of the competent authorities, you held two rifles in your home?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I handed in those guns to the SUP and they gave me time to submit another request to become a member of the hunting society and to have the right to possess the weapon, and I was rejected again.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you complain? Did you appeal the decision?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I did, and it was rejected. My wife appealed, and again it was rejected.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When were those weapons seized from you?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I think sometime in 1988 [Realtime transcript read in error "1998"]. I can't tell you the exact year.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: The seizure of weapons, as a result of that seizure, were you given a receipt on the type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What is Kratez? What kind of a rifle is Kratez?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a small error. Beganovic said "in 1988" and there's an error in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When was your rifle seized from you?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Around 1988, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you get a receipt? Because weapons were seized from you as you had possession of them illegally.

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does it say anything, that receipt?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: How can I remember what it says?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does it have a number of the rifle and name of it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Please don't be angry at me. I'm just asking you these things. Why does it say under number 2 "Kratez"? Did you ever have a shorter rifle?

utterances.speaker: EMIR BEGANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was a normal shotgun, .12 calibre, and a carbine, bought in Novi Sad at an exhibition of hunting weapons, with the latest sniper, one that can be used at night. And my father even had medals for capital deer that he had killed, so he had very good, high quality weapons. I don't know what you mean by "Kratez".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, I apologise for interrupting you but we have to close for today. Is that all right? We'll adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further to what I have said -- yes, the witness should come back again tomorrow. He's leaving us now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further to what I have said in relation to the pattern of two breaks of half an hour each, to give the accused time to rest as well, I would like to suggest the following timetable, which I would like you to note down: We start at 9.30. We will have a break at 11.00, and after a 30-minute break, which means the second slot of work will be from 11.30 until ten to one. And then again a half-hour break, and the third slot will be from 1.20 until 2.30. You see that we get tired as we move along, so we're shortening the working period. The first will be for an hour, thirty; the second one hour, twenty; and the third one hour, ten. So in total four working hours. Why am I saying this? I'm saying this for you to be able to manage your own time. You have questions to put, and my idea would be that it is not convenient to interrupt a question for the benefit of a break. If you only have one question, you will put it, but don't go on to the next question until after the break. So with these small differences, plus/minus five minutes, we are going to try to respect this timetable. And if you forget, I will give you the classical sign of time out. It is universally understood. I think everyone will know what I mean. The idea is to regulate and organise our work. We all know the rules, and the rule regarding the management of time would be as I have just described. But to guarantee that the accused has time to rest, we have had to change the timetable a little bit. So we're going to test it to see whether it works, and to do so, we will meet here again tomorrow at 9.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Could I quickly put the Court on notice of an issue with witnesses. Witness number 3, because of business commitments, we've had to change witness number 3 in the order, so we'll move up a witness. So instead of witness number 3, the person named as witness number 4 will move up into that position. The witness number 3 will be back with us next week and we will reinsert witness number 3 in the order. But because of that witness' business commitments that could not be changed, we've had to change that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Perhaps I should consult Mr. Simic, or someone else. Do you object to a change in the order of witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the standpoint of the Chamber, we understand very well that there is a certain order of the presentation of evidence, but it is possible to change it. The only thing is for the parties to be prepared and ready for the cross-examination. But the Chamber has no problem with it, and I see that the Defence does not object either. So thank you, Ms. Hollis. Until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: 2.40 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 5th day of May, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
